To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
autonomy and competence satisfaction are important predictors of job and life satisfaction through self efficacy.
autonomy satisfaction and self efficacy are important factors that influence university teachers' job satisfaction.

autonomy satisfaction and relatedness satisfaction are positively associated with self efficacy; self efficacy is positively associated with job satisfaction; job satisfaction is positively associated with life satisfaction; and self efficacy partially mediates the relationship between autonomy satisfaction and job satisfaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between BPNS and self efficacy, and how these two variables influence job and life satisfaction of university teachers.
the relationships between BPNS, self efficacy, job and life satisfaction, and the mediating role of self efficacy.
the well being of university teachers, a group that has received little attention in the literature on occupational well being.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the present study has successfully tested a conceptual process model in which the relationships among basic psychological needs satisfaction, self efficacy, job and life satisfaction were investigated.

university teachers who feel that they have the freedom to choose their own work methods (autonomy), and feel competent and effective in their teaching (competence) will have higher self efficacy, and higher self efficacy will lead to higher job satisfaction and higher job satisfaction will lead to higher life satisfaction.
university teachers' job satisfaction and life satisfaction are positively related to their self efficacy, autonomy satisfaction and competence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present study has demonstrated the important roles of BPNS and self efficacy in predicting university teachers' job satisfaction and life satisfaction.
the present study provides empirical evidence that university teachers' BPNS and self efficacy can predict their job and life satisfaction.
the present study provides a new perspective on how to promote teachers' job and personal well being.
The main takeaway from our work is that
university teachers' job satisfaction and life satisfaction are positively related to their basic psychological needs satisfaction, and self efficacy.

university teachers need to be given opportunities to satisfy their basic needs in order to be satisfied in their jobs and lives, and university managers can help them by providing autonomy, competence, relatedness, and self efficacy opportunities in the workplace.

the university teachers' job well-being and life well-being are not independent from each other, but rather they are interrelated through the mediating variables of self efficacy, job, and life satisfaction.
